findings.text: The harness does not clear `REQ_ROOT`. Root resolution is `--root`, then `REQ_ROOT`, then the nearest ancestor of the CWD (`src/root.rs`), so on a machine/CI where `REQ_ROOT` is exported every `req canon` here reads that corpus instead of the scratch dir. The exit-code contract these tests exist to pin then proves nothing: the flagged-pin tests redden or, worse, `a_clean_green_does_not_read_as_a_release_pass` goes green against a foreign clean corpus, and the unreadable-corpus test can exit 2/0 for unrelated reasons. This is exactly why `tests/init.rs` (`run_at`) and the other CLI fixtures call `.env_remove("REQ_ROOT")`.
findings.title: test

findings.text: When `--fail-on-flag` is passed with any additional argument (`req canon --fail-on-flag extra`, `req canon --fail-on-flag --verify`, or the flag twice), the guarded arm (`args.len() == 1`) does not match and the match falls through to `Some(other)`, printing `unrecognized flag: --fail-on-flag`. The exit code 2 is correct, but the message names the one valid flag as unrecognized and points the user at removing it instead of at the bad argument combination. The new `other_arguments_stay_usage_errors` test only asserts the usage line, so it does not catch this wording. Handle `Some("--fail-on-flag")` outside the guard (e.g. an "unexpected argument" arm) so the diagnostic names the actual problem.
findings.title: Misleading error

findings.text: The exit line contradicts itself: it says `req canon` "never gates" and in the same sentence describes `--fail-on-flag` exiting 1. Reword it so the default mode is report-only and the opt-in is the only mode that can fail, matching the behavior this PR adds.
findings.title: Fix contradictory help exit wording
findings.code:
exit: 0 diagnostics reported — not a pass: it reports, and it never gates; with `--fail-on-flag`,
0 means no pin is flagged and 1 means at least one is; 3 a registry or claim file that cannot be
read (or is NOT JUDGED); 2 usage, including `--fill` and `--verify`.
